title: juphyter
tagline: A Jupyter and Quarto kernel for PHP, built for statistical work with the phpstats packages.
summary: juphyter runs PHP cells in JupyterLab and in Quarto documents. It installs a Jupyter kernelspec, so JupyterLab lists PHP in its launcher and Quarto executes {php} blocks in a .qmd. It corresponds to IRkernel, which runs R in Jupyter, and to knitr, which executes R in Quarto and R Markdown.

A cell's last expression is its result, and that value is published in every representation the front end might draw. A phibble data frame arrives as an HTML table carrying its dimensions and its column types, a phiz plot as a Vega-Lite chart in a notebook and as a static SVG in a PDF, and any class can opt in with a toHtml() or a toMimeBundle() method. Juphyter\display() publishes a value part way through a cell, so one cell can show several tables or plots.

Session state carries from one cell to the next, including use statements and declared functions and classes, and a traceback names the cell and the line a stack frame came from rather than eval()'d code. The engine finds the nearest vendor/autoload.php by walking up from the notebook's own directory, so a notebook inside a Composer project sees that project's packages with nothing to configure, and --autoload or a juphyter.json entry names an autoloader for a notebook kept outside a project.

The kernel is a Python transport in front of a PHP engine. ipykernel speaks the Jupyter protocol and a PHP process runs the cells over a unix socket, which is why the install needs a Python with ipykernel in it as well as PHP. The engine runs on macOS and Linux, because interrupting a running cell uses POSIX signals. PHP can redeclare neither a class nor a function, so re-running a cell that declares one needs a kernel restart, and a cell cannot declare a namespace.
requires: PHP 8.3, 8.4, or 8.5, with the pcntl, posix, and sockets extensions; a phiz plot needs 8.5
Python 3 with ipykernel, which the kernel's transport runs inside
Quarto, to render Quarto documents; JupyterLab needs none of it
macOS or Linux, because a cell is interrupted with POSIX signals
The vl-convert binary, optional, for the static images a PDF or Word figure is made from
